--- title: "Randomized dynamic events" subtitle: "Part 4 · Drawing the disturbance itself" description: "Describe disturbances as a distribution, preview the draws on the grid graph, and generate a dataset where every sample meets a different event." jupyter: python3 --- ::: {.session-strip} [20 min]{.chip} [Part 4 of 4]{.chip} [Dynawo · gridfm-datakit]{.chip} ::: ::: {.goals} #### In this part - Write a distribution of disturbances in a few lines of configuration. - Preview the drawn events on the grid graph before simulating anything. - Generate trajectories under faults and trips, and read back what each sample went through. ::: ::: {#360d29a2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import json import shutil from pathlib import Path import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import pandas as pd import pypowsybl as pp import yaml import zarr work = Path("outputs/part4") shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) work.mkdir(parents=True) ``` ::: ## Events as a distribution Part 3 hit every operating point with the same fault. A model trained on that data learns one fault. `dynamic.event_perturbation` draws the events of every sample from **scenarios** you describe instead. - A scenario is a sequence of one or more events, drawn with a relative `weight`. - Each event has a `type`, a `target` and its `params`, plus an optional `delay` after the scenario's `start_time`. - A target is either a fixed `static_id`, or an element type at a `distance` in branch hops from an **anchor** bus, itself fixed or random. - Any number can be a **value spec**, a fixed value or a distribution. | Value spec | Draw | |---|---| | `0.1` | always 0.1 | | `{distribution: uniform, low, high}` | uniform on `[low, high)` | | `{distribution: normal, mean, std, min, max}` | normal, redrawn outside the bounds | | `{distribution: choice, values, weights}` | one of the values | | Event type | Targets | Parameters | |---|---|---| | `NodeFault` | bus | `fault_time`, `r_pu`, `x_pu` | | `Disconnect` | bus, generator, load, line, transformer | none | | `ActivePowerVariation` | generator, load | `delta_p` | | `ReactivePowerVariation` | generator, load | `delta_q` | | `ReferenceVoltageVariation` | generator | `delta_u` | ## Four kinds of trouble A bus fault cleared after a delay, a line trip, a bus fault with a line tripping next to it, and the loss of a generator. The plain bus fault is twice as likely as each of the others. ::: {#d7236944 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} event_perturbation = yaml.safe_load(""" type: random n_event_variants: 4 # event variants per operating point scenarios: - name: bus_fault weight: 2 start_time: {distribution: uniform, low: 0.5, high: 2.0} events: - type: NodeFault target: {element: bus, distance: 0} params: fault_time: {distribution: normal, mean: 0.1, std: 0.03, min: 0.05, max: 0.2} r_pu: 0.0 x_pu: {distribution: uniform, low: 0.005, high: 0.05} - name: line_trip start_time: {distribution: uniform, low: 0.5, high: 2.0} events: - type: Disconnect target: {element: line, distance: [0, 2]} - name: fault_and_line_trip start_time: {distribution: uniform, low: 0.5, high: 2.0} events: - type: NodeFault target: {element: bus, distance: 0} params: fault_time: 0.2 r_pu: 0.0 x_pu: {distribution: uniform, low: 0.005, high: 0.05} - type: Disconnect target: {element: line, distance: 0} delay: {distribution: uniform, low: 0.08, high: 0.15} - name: generator_trip start_time: {distribution: uniform, low: 0.5, high: 2.0} events: - type: Disconnect target: {element: generator, distance: [0, 3]} """) ``` ::: `distance: 0` from a random anchor picks any bus. In `fault_and_line_trip`, the line at distance 0 touches the faulted bus. It trips 80 to 150 ms after the fault starts, and the fault still lasts its full 200 ms. ## Preview the draws The draw happens on the graph of the grid, so it can be inspected without running Dynawo. Datakit calls the same functions inside the pipeline, seeded per sample. ::: {#73ec7420 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} from gridfm_datakit.dynamic.event_perturbation import draw_events, parse_event_perturbation from gridfm_datakit.dynamic.placement import EventGraph network = pp.network.load("../data/ieee14/IEEE14.iidm") graph = EventGraph.from_network(network) spec = parse_event_perturbation(event_perturbation, start_time=0.0, stop_time=10.0) rng = np.random.default_rng(7) preview = pd.concat( [draw_events(spec, graph, rng).assign(draw=i) for i in range(8)], ignore_index=True ) preview.round(3).set_index(["draw", "scenario"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Every row is an event Dynawo will simulate, with its time and its drawn parameters written out. ## Generate Six load scenarios, no topology change so that the events stand out, four event variants each. The configuration is the one from Part 3 with `event_perturbation` added, a shorter list of curves, and its own output folder. ::: {#9e545ae0 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} variables = pd.DataFrame( [("Curve", f"_BUS{'_' * (5 - len(str(i)))}{i}_TN", "U_value") for i in range(1, 15)] + [("Curve", "_GEN____1_SM", "generator_omegaPu_value")], columns=["type", "model_id", "variables"], ) variables.to_csv(work / "variables.csv", index=False) config = yaml.safe_load(""" network: name: IEEE14 source: file reader: powsybl file: ../data/ieee14/IEEE14.iidm load: generator: agg_load_profile agg_profile: default scenarios: 6 sigma: 0.2 change_reactive_power: true global_range: 0.4 max_scaling_factor: 4.0 step_size: 0.05 start_scaling_factor: 0.8 topology_perturbation: type: none generation_perturbation: type: none admittance_perturbation: type: none dynamic: dynamic_solver: dynawo input_files: static_element_dynamic_models_file: ../data/ieee14/static_element_dynamic_models.csv automation_systems_file: ../data/ieee14/automation_systems.csv variables_file: outputs/part4/variables.csv solver_parameters: start_time: 0.0 stop_time: 10.0 parameters_file: ../data/ieee14/IEEE14.par network_parameters_file: ../data/ieee14/IEEE14.par network_parameters_id: Network solver_type: IDA solver_parameters_file: ../data/ieee14/IEEE14.par solver_parameters_id: IDAOrder2 logging: verbosity: warning settings: mode: pf pf_solver: powsybl data_dir: outputs/part4/data num_processes: 4 large_chunk_size: 6 overwrite: true include_dc_res: false enable_solver_logs: false pf_fast: false dcpf_fast: false max_iter: 200 seed: 42 """) config["dynamic"]["event_perturbation"] = event_perturbation ``` ::: ::: {#68faa0b0 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} from gridfm_datakit.dynamic.generate_dynamic import generate_dynamic_data generate_dynamic_data(config) ``` ::: ## What each sample went through `events.parquet` records every simulated event, keyed like the curves. ::: {#74e474c2 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} root = Path("outputs/part4/data/IEEE14/raw/dynamic") KEYS = ["scenario_index", "perturbation_index", "event_index"] events = pd.read_parquet(root / "events.parquet") meta = json.loads((root / "metadata.json").read_text()) store = zarr.open(str(root / "dynamic_results.zarr"), mode="r") bus = pd.read_parquet(root / "bus_data.parquet") slice_of = { tuple(int(v) for v in key): i for i, key in enumerate(zip(*(np.asarray(store[k]) for k in KEYS))) } def curve(key, name): """Time and values of one variable for one sample, without the NaN padding.""" i = slice_of[key] n = meta["timesteps_per_scenario"][i] return store["time"][i, :n], store["curves"][i, meta["variable_names"].index(name), :n] print(len(slice_of), "samples") events.round(3).head(8) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 24 samples ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}

The lowest bus voltage across the grid, relative to its value before the event, shows how deep each disturbance cut. ::: {#eea7cf46 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} u_names = [name for name in meta["variable_names"] if name.endswith("U_value")] names = [s["name"] for s in event_perturbation["scenarios"]] fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 6.4), sharex=True, sharey=True) for ax, name, color in zip(axes.flat, names, PALETTE): for key in [k for k in slice_of if kind.get(k) == name]: t = curve(key, u_names[0])[0] u = np.array([curve(key, n)[1] for n in u_names]) ax.plot(t, (u / u[:, :1]).min(axis=0), color=color, linewidth=1.2, alpha=0.8) ax.set(title=name.replace("_", " "), xlim=(0, 6)) for ax in axes[1]: ax.set_xlabel("time (s)") for ax in axes[:, 0]: ax.set_ylabel("lowest bus voltage\n(pu of initial)") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](04-dynamic-events_files/figure-html/cell-10-output-1.png){width=1090 height=693} ::: ::: Faults dip deep and recover. Trips leave a lasting change. A fault with a line trip does both. When the faulted bus hangs on a single line, the trip leaves it dead, which is the flat line at zero. ## Initial state, event, trajectory Every sample now holds three aligned pieces: the Parquet initial state, the event record and the Zarr trajectory. Add the `topology_perturbation` of Part 3 and all three keys vary at once. ::: {#61e3a307 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} key = list(slice_of)[5] print("sample", dict(zip(KEYS, key))) print("initial demand", round(bus.set_index(KEYS).loc[key].Pd.sum(), 1), "MW") events.set_index(KEYS).loc[[key], ["scenario", "event_name", "static_id", "start_time", "params"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` sample {'scenario_index': 1, 'perturbation_index': 0, 'event_index': 1} initial demand 428.7 MW ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Your turn ::: {.callout-tip .exercise title="Exercise · A fixed hot spot"} Add a fifth scenario, `voltage_step`, that changes the voltage set-point of generator 1 (`static_id: _GEN____1_SM`) by a value drawn uniformly between -0.05 and 0.05 pu. Preview twenty draws with the new spec and count how often each scenario comes up. ::: ::: {.callout-note .solution collapse="true" title="Show a solution"} ::: {#a7fbb16e .cell tags='["solution"]' execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} voltage_step = yaml.safe_load(""" name: voltage_step start_time: {distribution: uniform, low: 0.5, high: 2.0} events: - type: ReferenceVoltageVariation target: {static_id: _GEN____1_SM} params: delta_u: {distribution: uniform, low: -0.05, high: 0.05} """) extended = {**event_perturbation, "scenarios": event_perturbation["scenarios"] + [voltage_step]} spec = parse_event_perturbation(extended, start_time=0.0, stop_time=10.0) rng = np.random.default_rng(0) draws = [draw_events(spec, graph, rng) for _ in range(20)] pd.Series([d.scenario.iloc[0] for d in draws]).value_counts() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11} ``` fault_and_line_trip 6 line_trip 6 voltage_step 3 bus_fault 3 generator_trip 2 Name: count, dtype: int64 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note title="Where to go next"} The [dynamic simulation manual](https://github.com/yemine0x01/gridfm-datakit/blob/gfm6wt/docs/manual/dynamic_simulation.md) of GridFM-Datakit documents every key, the output layout and the known limits.
